title: Protect one trip while a region degrades
description: Inject a dispatch, freshness, regional, or duplicate-command failure, then choose a recovery policy. The lab shows which path remains authoritative and what the rider actually experiences.

nodes.label: Regional gateway
nodes.responsibility: Admits rider and driver commands into the rider's home region.

nodes.label: Location index
nodes.responsibility: Holds expiring driver coordinates for nearby-candidate search.

nodes.label: Dispatch
nodes.responsibility: Scores candidates and creates bounded driver offers.

nodes.label: Trip authority
nodes.responsibility: Serializes the trip state, assigned driver, and version.

nodes.label: Regional event log
nodes.responsibility: Publishes committed trip changes for local consumers and replay.

nodes.label: Peer region
nodes.responsibility: Receives asynchronous summaries without owning the active trip.

responses.label: Retry through every path
responses.detail: Keep sending the command to local and remote dependencies until one answers.

responses.label: Gate and isolate
responses.detail: Reject unsafe inputs, fence the affected boundary, and preserve a local authoritative state.

responses.label: Replay by identity and version
responses.detail: Retry the durable command with the same key and expected trip version.

scenarios.label: Dispatch service unavailable
scenarios.detail: Candidate scoring times out before any driver offer is committed.

retry-everywhere.title: Retries turn one dispatch outage into regional overload
retry-everywhere.detail: The request fans out while the scoring dependency is still unavailable. Queues grow, remote capacity is consumed, and the rider still has no authoritative assignment.

gate-and-isolate.title: The rider sees a bounded delay and trip state stays clean
gate-and-isolate.detail: The gateway stops new offers in the affected cell, keeps the trip requested, and returns a retryable unavailable result instead of inventing an assignment.

idempotent-replay.title: Replay is safe but cannot replace a failed scorer
idempotent-replay.detail: Stable identity prevents duplicate trip writes, yet no candidate can be selected until dispatch recovers or traffic moves to a rehearsed local fallback.

scenarios.label: Driver location is stale
scenarios.detail: A candidate has not published a coordinate within the location freshness bound.

retry-everywhere.title: A ghost candidate produces a bad pickup promise
retry-everywhere.detail: Retrying the same stale coordinate makes it look available without making it true. The rider can receive an offer for a driver who has moved or gone offline.

gate-and-isolate.title: Freshness wins over a fast but false match
gate-and-isolate.detail: Dispatch removes the stale driver, expands within the bounded regional search policy, and reports a longer wait if no fresh candidate remains.

idempotent-replay.title: Command identity cannot make a coordinate fresh
idempotent-replay.detail: The replay is deduplicated, but the original candidate evidence is still outside its freshness bound. The location must be refreshed or excluded.

scenarios.label: Region loses its peer link
scenarios.detail: The active region can reach local trip storage but cannot replicate events to a peer.

retry-everywhere.title: Cross-region retries threaten two writers for one trip
retry-everywhere.detail: Routing active-trip commands to a peer without transferring ownership can create competing state histories while the replication link is uncertain.

gate-and-isolate.title: Local trips continue and replication waits behind a fence
gate-and-isolate.detail: The home region remains the only writer, stores local events durably, and queues peer replication. Cross-region analytics may be stale, but the rider and driver share one trip state.

idempotent-replay.title: Replay must wait until regional ownership is fenced
idempotent-replay.detail: Stable event IDs help reconciliation, but replaying into an unfenced peer can still apply legal-looking transitions under the wrong regional owner.

scenarios.label: Assignment acknowledgement is lost
scenarios.detail: The trip commit succeeded, but dispatch timed out and retries the assignment command.

retry-everywhere.title: A new retry identity can repeat assignment side effects
retry-everywhere.detail: The trip is already assigned. Treating the timeout as a new command can notify another driver, charge twice, or publish a second assignment event.

gate-and-isolate.title: Stopping retries protects consumers but leaves uncertainty
gate-and-isolate.detail: The caller avoids another side effect, yet it still needs to read the authoritative trip by command identity to learn whether the assignment committed.

idempotent-replay.title: The same command returns the committed assignment
idempotent-replay.detail: Trip authority recognizes the idempotency key and expected version, returns the existing result, and emits no second assignment side effect.
idempotent-replay.tripState: assigned v18, duplicate is a no-op
